{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABZiXe4w", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhDJKYY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 63, "title": "Add standard clocked cassette playback through MSX PSG/PPI and local CAS loading", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `3bf1359b15a7cd717d21776af54886887f34b27d`, PSG R14 bit 7 always reads low. PPI port-C writes retain control bits, but no cassette medium or playback clock exists. Software polling the cassette signal therefore cannot load tape data. See [current hardware I/O and scheduling](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/blob/3bf1359b15a7cd717d21776af54886887f34b27d/crates/msx-core/src/lib.rs).

This excludes tape-distributed software from the commercial-readiness goal. Implement standard playback as one complete core/Wasm/browser capability, with independently authored diagnostics. No commercial tape has been observed working.

## Expected outcome

MSX1 and MSX2 software can receive standard cassette bytes by executing Z80 reads of the actual PSG input, with playback controlled by the PPI motor signal. Users can mount a local MSX CAS image at 1200 baud by default or select 2400 baud, inspect transport status, rewind and eject.

Scope includes standard CAS reconstruction and read-only playback. Recording, WAV/TSX, exotic loaders, analog degradation, audible tape monitoring and Weave BASIC cassette commands are deferred. Preserve supplied-firmware execution without BIOS interception or direct payload injection.

## Context

- The [MSX2 Technical Handbook, chapter 5](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Konamiman/MSX2-Technical-Handbook/master/md/Chapter5a.md), sections 2.1–2.5, describes standard rates, CPU-timed pulses, LSB-first framing and leaders. Its paragraph naming PSG R15 as cassette input conflicts with its own R14 example; use the corroborated wiring below.
- Pinned upstream [MSXPSG](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/sound/MSXPSG.cc) places cassette input on R14.7. [MSXPPI](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/MSXPPI.cc) establishes active-low C4 motor control.
- [CasImage](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/cassette/CasImage.cc) supplies a behavioral reference for MSX CAS markers and standard file-block reconstruction. Its accelerated 3744-baud playback is an emulator policy with explicit uncertainties; use the standard rates here. [CassettePlayer](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/cassette/CassettePlayer.cc) corroborates motor-controlled position and signal sampling. No upstream runtime comparison was performed.
- CAS does not preserve the original waveform, speed or exact gaps. Document reconstruction choices as policies, including silence durations, initial polarity and unknown-block handling.
- Open Issues are empty. Cassette/tape history searches found earlier scope exclusions, without a dedicated implementation. PR #62 concerns disk behavior. Its [saved validation](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/blob/3bf1359b15a7cd717d21776af54886887f34b27d/docs/validation.md) reports 252 Rust and 162 browser passes; inspected CI step metadata marks the relevant checks successful. These existing results contain no cassette-loading coverage. No builds or tests were rerun during planning.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement bounded, validated MSX CAS parsing and deterministic playback. Recognize the `1F A6 DE BA CC 13 7D 74` block marker without transmitting it. Preserve payload bytes, standard binary/tokenized-BASIC/ASCII file sequences, multiple files and ASCII continuation blocks. Reconstruct appropriate long/short leaders; preserve unknown data-block contents with a documented conservative leader policy. Reject empty, malformed or unsupported inputs without silently discarding data or changing the previous session. Document the marker format’s inherent ambiguities.
- [ ] Generate one zero start bit, eight LSB-first data bits and two one stop bits. At 1200 baud, zero uses one 1200-Hz cycle and one uses two 2400-Hz cycles; double these frequencies at 2400 baud. Long leaders contain 16000/32000 high-frequency cycles and short leaders 4000/8000 respectively. Use emulated CPU time with retained fractional timing so rounding cannot accumulate drift; avoid expanding every pulse into an unnecessarily large waveform buffer.
- [ ] Route playback exclusively into PSG R14.7 and honor active-low PPI C4 through both direct AAh writes and ABh bit-set/reset writes. Motor-off freezes position and fractional phase, returns idle-low input, and resumes without skipping data. Silence, no medium and end-of-tape return idle low; end-of-tape stops without wrapping. Preserve R14 bits 0–6, both joystick connectors/common lines, existing PSG direction policy, keyboard row selection and unrelated PPI bits. A general 8255 rewrite is outside scope.
- [ ] Define and test transport lifecycle: mount/replacement starts the new image at its beginning without resetting CPU or changing firmware; rewind resets only tape position/phase; eject removes the medium without resetting execution. Reset retains mounted bytes, selected rate and position, and consistently reapplies the reset PPI motor latch. Firmware/model transitions retain the medium and position with the same reset policy. No automatic rewind or load-command injection.
- [ ] Extend the existing staged Wasm upload/error pattern and browser controls for local CAS loading, rate choice, rewind, eject and meaningful mounted/motor/end status. Freeze tape when emulation is paused. Reject invalid rates, allocation/size failures, canceled imports and stale asynchronous completions transactionally. Keep local bytes private and transient, and preserve existing cartridge/SRAM, firmware, disk and audio state through tape-only operations.
- [ ] Add independent native pulse/framing expectations covering `00`, `FF`, `55`, `AA`, high-bit bytes, leaders, gaps, block boundaries and terminal data. Derive expected timestamps from explicit clock/rate arithmetic, independently of production encoding helpers. Compare single-cycle, irregular and large tick partitions, including motor changes mid-pulse, long playback, rewind, reset, end-of-tape and malformed imports. Demonstrate a meaningful cassette-input/loading failure against the baseline; report the observed result.
- [ ] Add original, redistributable Z80 loader diagnostics on both models and rates. Through ordinary PSG/PPI I/O, measure leaders, decode complete header/body payloads into RAM, stop/resume the motor and execute a recovered payload producing a checked visible result. Assert exact recovered bytes, not only a checksum or status label. Exercise compiled Wasm through the real browser file picker at both `/` and `/msx-rust/`, including transport and failed/stale-import behavior. Use bounded timeouts and no host-provided decoded bytes, BIOS traps or proprietary firmware.
- [ ] Update user guidance, hardware limits, fixture source/provenance and build/distribution inventory where affected. Explain that C-BIOS/Weave BASIC do not thereby gain a complete BASIC tape-loading environment. Preserve existing MSX1/MSX2, audio, disk, SRAM, firmware, browser/Wasm and ownership behavior. Diagnostic success must not be reported as commercial-title compatibility.
- [ ] The Coordinator must run and report `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs` and `npm test`, using README setup prerequisites as needed. Complete source-Issue/full-diff review and resolve blocking findings before merge under repository guidance. Distinguish passing, failing, skipped and unperformed checks accurately.

## Optional validation

Compare original pulse vectors and the diagnostic loader against a pinned upstream emulator. If suitable firmware or tapes are already lawfully available, observe genuine BIOS loading and representative software, recording exact inputs and results. These checks were not performed and are not prerequisites; no proprietary acquisition or human gameplay is required.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
